```{r setup, include=FALSE}
.libPaths(c("Rlib", .libPaths()))
library(plotly)
data("ToothGrowth", package = "datasets")
tg <- ToothGrowth
tg$dose_display <- tg$dose + ifelse(tg$supp == "OJ", -0.035, 0.035)
tg$animal <- paste("Guinea pig", seq_len(nrow(tg)))
means <- aggregate(len ~ dose + supp, tg, mean)

chart <- plot_ly() |>
  add_trace(data = tg, x = ~dose_display, y = ~len, type = "scatter", mode = "markers",
            color = ~supp, colors = c("#35C2B7", "#FFB657"),
            text = ~paste0(animal, "<br>Supplement: ", supp,
                           "<br>Dose: ", dose, " mg/day<br>Tooth length: ", len),
            hovertemplate = "%{text}<extra></extra>",
            marker = list(size = 8, opacity = 0.48, line = list(width = 0)),
            showlegend = TRUE)
chart <- chart |>
  add_trace(data = means, x = ~dose, y = ~len, type = "scatter", mode = "lines+markers",
            color = ~supp, colors = c("#35C2B7", "#FFB657"),
            text = ~paste0(supp, " mean<br>Dose: ", dose,
                           " mg/day<br>Mean length: ", round(len, 2)),
            hovertemplate = "%{text}<extra></extra>",
            marker = list(size = 12, line = list(color = "#102B3F", width = 2)),
            line = list(width = 3), showlegend = FALSE)
chart <- chart |>
  layout(xaxis = list(title = "Vitamin C dose (mg/day)", tickmode = "array",
                      tickvals = c(0.5, 1, 2), ticktext = c("0.5", "1", "2"),
                      range = c(0.35, 2.15), gridcolor = "#243D50", zeroline = FALSE),
         yaxis = list(title = "Tooth length", range = c(0, 35),
                      gridcolor = "#243D50", zeroline = FALSE),
         paper_bgcolor = "rgba(0,0,0,0)", plot_bgcolor = "rgba(0,0,0,0)",
         font = list(family = "Arial", color = "#EAF3F5"),
         legend = list(title = list(text = "Supplement"), orientation = "h",
                       x = 0, y = 1.12), hovermode = "closest")
chart_json <- plotly_json(chart, jsonedit = FALSE)
```

<div class="deck">
  <header class="topline"><span class="brand"><i class="dot"></i> Data in motion / field note 01</span><span>ToothGrowth · 60 animals</span></header>

      <div class="eyebrow">A tiny experiment, an interactive view</div>

      <div class="date-pill"><span class="dot"></span> Created October 28, 2026 <span style="color:var(--muted)">· R Markdown + Plotly</span></div>
      <p class="footnote">Swipe with the arrow keys or use the controls below.</p>
    </section>

    <section class="slide" aria-label="Slide 2: interactive chart">
      <div class="eyebrow">01 / Explore the measurements</div>
      <h2>More dose, longer teeth.<br>At the top dose, the methods meet.</h2>
      <p>Each point is one guinea pig. Hover for its dose, supplement, and tooth length; the larger connected markers show group means.</p>
      <div class="slide-grid">
        <div class="chart-card"><div id="tooth-chart" role="img" aria-label="Interactive Plotly chart of tooth length by vitamin C dose and supplement"></div></div>
        <aside class="insight-card">
          <span class="tag">At 2 mg/day</span>
          <div class="big-stat">26.06 <span style="font-size:1.2rem;color:var(--muted)">vs</span> 26.14</div>
          <p>Mean tooth length for orange juice and ascorbic acid, respectively.</p>
          <p class="small">The gap that appears at lower doses has nearly disappeared here. Select or hide legend entries to compare patterns.</p>
        </aside>
      </div>
      <p class="footnote">Source: R's built-in <code>datasets::ToothGrowth</code>. Doses are 0.5, 1, and 2 mg/day; n = 10 per dose × supplement group.</p>
    </section>

    <section class="slide" aria-label="Slide 3: takeaways">
      <div class="eyebrow">02 / The takeaway</div>
      <h2>A clear dose gradient.<br>A subtler supplement story.</h2>
      <div class="takeaways">
        <article class="stat-card"><h3>At 0.5 mg/day</h3><strong>13.23 vs 7.98</strong><p>OJ mean is higher than VC by 5.25 tooth-length units.</p></article>
        <article class="stat-card"><h3>At 1 mg/day</h3><strong>22.70 vs 16.77</strong><p>The OJ–VC difference is 5.93 units.</p></article>
        <article class="stat-card"><h3>Across doses</h3><strong>Both rise</strong><p>Mean tooth length increases from 0.5 to 2 mg/day for both methods.</p></article>
      </div>
      <div class="closing">
        <div><span class="tag">Read the design, too</span><p>There are just 10 animals in each group. These measurements illustrate a pattern in this experiment; they are not, by themselves, a broad claim about every animal or dose.</p></div>
        <div class="note-box"><p><strong>One visual question to keep:</strong><br>Does the apparent convergence at the highest dose reflect a real difference in response, or ordinary variation in a small sample?</p></div>
      </div>

</script>
<script>
(() => {
  const slides = [...document.querySelectorAll('.slide')];
  const previous = document.getElementById('prev');
  const next = document.getElementById('next');
  const counter = document.getElementById('counter');
  const progress = document.getElementById('progress');
  let current = 0, plotted = false;
  function show(index) {
    current = Math.max(0, Math.min(slides.length - 1, index));
    slides.forEach((slide, i) => slide.classList.toggle('active', i === current));
    previous.disabled = current === 0; next.disabled = current === slides.length - 1;
    counter.textContent = `${current + 1} / ${slides.length}`;
    progress.style.width = `${100 * (current + 1) / slides.length}%`;
    if (current === 1) {
      if (!plotted) {
        const spec = JSON.parse(document.getElementById('plot-spec').textContent);
        Plotly.newPlot('tooth-chart', spec.data, spec.layout,
          {responsive:true, displaylogo:false, scrollZoom:true});
        plotted = true;
      } else Plotly.Plots.resize(document.getElementById('tooth-chart'));
    }
    window.scrollTo({top:0, behavior:'smooth'});
  }
  previous.addEventListener('click', () => show(current - 1));
  next.addEventListener('click', () => show(current + 1));
  document.addEventListener('keydown', event => {
    if (event.key === 'ArrowRight' || event.key === 'PageDown') show(current + 1);
    if (event.key === 'ArrowLeft' || event.key === 'PageUp') show(current - 1);
  });
  show(0);
})();
</script>
</body>
